headline: Copper sinks to a five-week low as London warehouse stocks swell
detail: COMEX copper fell about 2.8% Thursday to roughly $6.40 a pound and London copper hit its lowest since mid-September as LME stocks rose a fourth day to the highest since July, much of it metal moving out of US warehouses. Expect copper scrap bids to soften.

headline: Scrap dealers and mills expect higher ferrous prices in November
detail: Market players told Steel Market Update that US ferrous scrap will probably rise again in November after October settled up $20-30 a ton, with supply tight and mills busy. Flows usually slow heading into winter, which supports prices.

headline: Big Daddy trims copper and aluminum bids
detail: Big Daddy Scrap in Chicago Heights cut bare bright to $5.43 a pound (from $5.52), #1 copper to $5.37 and cans to $0.45, while ferrous prices held steady. The Alsip-area average for #1 copper slipped to about $4.76.

headline: Teck copper mine strike could start Saturday
detail: The union at Teck's Highland Valley mine in British Columbia, which made about 127,000 tons of copper last year, can strike from Saturday morning if no deal is reached. A walkout would tighten North American copper supply and could lift prices.

headline: Gold drops to a two-month low, silver falls nearly 6%
detail: Gold fell about 2.9% to near $4,020 an ounce and silver lost almost 6% to around $54 as higher oil fed inflation fears and bets on another Fed hike. A stronger rate outlook tends to weigh on all metals.

headline: Platinum and palladium hit multi-month lows
detail: Platinum fell to its lowest since late July and palladium to its lowest since June 2025 during Thursday's selloff. Lower PGM prices mean lower values for catalytic converters.

headline: Traders see an 86% chance of a December Fed hike
detail: Futures now price a strong chance the Fed raises rates again in December after hot inflation data; the Fed meets Oct. 27–28 and is expected to hold for now. Higher rates and a firmer dollar are a headwind for metal prices.

headline: Gulf attacks push Brent near $112
detail: Brent rose almost 3% to about $112 Thursday after Iran claimed strikes on tankers near Hormuz, a drone strike hit Saudi Arabia's Shaybah oil field, and the US ordered nonessential staff out of Saudi Arabia. Higher energy costs raise smelting costs and inflation fears that weigh on metals.

headline: US-Mexico deal still stuck on 50% steel and aluminum tariffs
detail: Both sides say a deal is close, but Mexico wants cuts to the 50% metal tariffs and the 25% auto tariff, and an announcement may slip past the Nov. 3 midterms. Tariffs staying high keeps US metal prices above world levels.

headline: Iron ore touches its lowest in nearly two years
detail: Singapore iron ore futures dropped as much as 1.7% to about $89 a ton Thursday as Chinese port stocks keep building. Cheap ore helps blast-furnace mills compete with scrap-based mills.

headline: Nucor raises spot hot-rolled coil to $1,255 a ton
detail: Nucor lifted its weekly HRC price $15 to $1,255 per short ton and California Steel went to $1,320, with lead times still three to five weeks. Rising steel prices help mills keep buying scrap.

headline: Steel Dynamics sees steady scrap, strong steel
detail: On its Oct 20 call the big mill said scrap cost it $404 a ton last quarter, down $8, and it expects scrap prices to stay fairly flat with plenty of obsolete scrap and soft exports. Steel demand is strong: record shipments, lead times into 2027 and Q4 mill outages tightening supply.

headline: Nickel settles up 3% on Indonesia output-cut talk
detail: LME nickel's official cash price jumped about 3% to $15,830 a ton Wednesday as Chinese producers in Indonesia discussed cutting output together, though it gave back about 1% overnight. A similar attempt failed in August, so the gain could fade.

headline: China aluminum stocks at a four-year seasonal low
detail: Chinese aluminum ingot and billet stocks kept falling this week, but SMM expects new smelters outside China to loosen supply into 2027. That points to steady near-term aluminum prices with downside later.

headline: Gulf smelter restart lifts aluminum supply
detail: Emirates Global Aluminium has brought back half the capacity at its war-damaged main smelter and aims for full output by early 2027. Aluminum still rose about 1% Wednesday to about $3,031 a ton.

headline: China's copper imports bounce back in September
detail: China imported about 255,000 tons of refined copper in September, up 21% from August but still down 24% from a year earlier. Steadier Chinese buying gives copper some support.

headline: Single-family home building hits a one-year low
detail: September single-family starts fell 4.6% and permits fell to their lowest since March 2023, while total starts dropped 5.2%. Less home building means less demand for copper wire, pipe and steel.

headline: Homebuilder confidence sinks to lowest since 2012
detail: The NAHB builder index fell to 29 in October as 30-year mortgage rates hit about 7.4%, and 43% of builders cut prices. Weak home building means less demand for copper wire, plumbing and steel.

headline: GM plans $20 billion buyback, will close Brownstown battery plant
detail: GM earned $3.3 billion in Q3, approved another $20 billion of stock buybacks and confirmed its Brownstown, Michigan battery plant will close in 2027. Slower EV plans mean less battery metal demand.

headline: Century Aluminum pushes to keep Section 232 tariffs
detail: Century's CEO urged keeping the 50% steel and aluminum tariffs in US-Mexico trade talks, and Commerce Secretary Lutnick reportedly opposes cutting them. Keeping tariffs supports high US aluminum and steel prices.

headline: National scrap index: copper and aluminum grades dip, ferrous flat
detail: The weekly index showed clean copper scrap down about 2 cents a pound and aluminum scrap grades down about 2%, while HMS, shred and busheling held unchanged. US steel mill output was up 4% from a year ago.

headline: China's economy grows 4.5% but property keeps sinking
detail: China's Q3 growth beat forecasts on strong exports and September factory output rose 5.5%, but property investment is down about 21% this year. Weak building in China limits demand for steel and copper.

headline: China steel output down 2.9% this year, exports steady
detail: China made 2.9% less crude steel in January through September, but September exports rose 3.3% from August to about 10.5 million tons. Steady Chinese exports keep pressure on world steel prices.

headline: Tesla profit drops 43% on flat sales
detail: Tesla's Q3 revenue was flat at about $28 billion and net income fell 43%, while battery storage installs missed estimates. It is a mixed signal for EV-related copper, nickel and aluminum demand.

headline: GM to add hybrids as fuel prices climb
detail: GM plans more hybrid models as high gas prices drive demand. Hybrids still use catalytic converters, which supports platinum, palladium and rhodium demand.

headline: Corvette plant adds a four-week December shutdown
detail: GM's Bowling Green Corvette plant will close for four more weeks in December, its 11th down week this year, with earlier stops blamed on parts shortages. Fewer cars built means less factory scrap.

headline: CIBC cuts its gold forecast
detail: CIBC lowered its Q4 gold forecast to $4,500 an ounce, far below its $6,500 start-of-year call, but still sees $5,200 on average in 2027. Gold has fallen three of the last four sessions on rate-hike worries.

headline: China defends rare-earth limits as Japan runs short
detail: Beijing defended its rare-earth export limits on Japan, which reportedly could run out of yttrium within months. Shortages could disrupt car, jet engine and chip production.
